dedupe_keys.name: omx open matrix file format for transport model matrices hdf5 based

description: OMX, the Open Matrix format, is an open file specification for storing the origin-destination matrices that transport demand models produce and exchange, such as trip tables and travel time skims. It is published by the osPlanning community on GitHub, which hopes the modelling industry will adopt it. Coverage: an OMX file is a structured collection of two-dimensional arrays with associated metadata, built on the HDF5 scientific storage standard, with a fixed layout meant to keep matrix data complete, consistent and efficiently readable. Format and access: the specification and wiki are on GitHub, with separate API libraries for Python, R, C#, C++, Java and Free Pascal; the wiki explains import and export with EMME, VISUM, TransCAD and Cube and links an online validator and viewer; free. Licence: Apache-2.0 for all OMX code and API implementations, as stated in the readme. Caveats: the main specification repository was last changed in May 2020, the earlier Google site and mailing list are no longer maintained, and OMX holds no data of its own, only the container. Simulation uses: exchanging demand and skim matrices between modelling packages for network flow, capacity planning and agent-based travel demand studies. Related records: EMME (model-bentley-openpaths-emme), PTV Visum (model-ptv-visum), TransCAD (model-transcad) and ActivitySim (model-activitysim) read or write OMX matrices.
